passages.title: A Week of Small Routines
passages.text:
Last week my brother Minh, a junior accountant, finally admitted that his daily habits needed fixing. On Monday he **had a late night** finishing a report, and by Tuesday he could hardly keep his eyes open. At lunchtime he only had time for **a light lunch**, a salad from the canteen, and then he tried to **have a sleep** on the sofa in the staff room, but his boss walked in. After that embarrassing moment, he decided to **have an early night** on Wednesday. He turned off the lights at nine and managed to **fall asleep** within minutes.

The mornings were another problem. Minh used to wake up late, so he would only **have a quick wash** and rush out of the house without breakfast. His girlfriend joked that he should at least **have a shave** before meetings, because he looked tired and untidy. At the weekend they shared the housework. She offered to **do the washing**, and he agreed to **do the ironing** because his shirts were a disaster. They also had to **do the shopping**, so they wrote a list and went to the market together. In the evening it rained heavily, and they preferred to **stay in** rather than go out. Neither of them felt like cooking, so they decided to **order a takeaway** and watch a film. "Maybe good habits start with small steps," Minh said.

passages.title: The Price of Winning
passages.text:
When my older brother Tuan became a national **sportsman**, our whole family changed. I am not proud of it, but I felt **jealousy** every time the neighbours praised him. I **assumed** that our parents loved him more, because they spent so much money on his training and drove him to every competition. Tuan's life looked perfect from the outside, yet his **position** as team captain was extremely **stressful**. He was often **stressed** before big matches and barely spoke to anyone at home.

Last year we had a terrible argument. **In the heat of the moment**, I told him he was selfish and never **bothered to ask** how I was doing. He shouted back that it was the **absolute last time** he would listen to my complaints. For weeks we did not speak.

Everything changed when his wife **gave birth** to a baby girl in March. Suddenly the famous athlete was learning how to **feed** a newborn at three in the morning, looking completely lost. I went to help, and we ended up laughing together for the first time in months. He admitted that he had been lonely, and I admitted my **jealousy**. Now we meet every weekend, and I no longer compare myself with him.

passages.title: Choosing Where to Live in Da Nang
passages.text:
Choosing where to live is not only about the price of the flat. Lan, a student in Da Nang, found a room in a district that is **a mix of** old family houses and modern cafés. Her university is **just around the corner from** her building, so she can walk to class. **There's a cheap noodle shop around the corner**, and a **cash machine** outside the supermarket, which is useful because many stalls do not accept cards. The long beach **stretches** for kilometres, and at weekends there are always events **going on** along the seafront, so she never feels bored.

Lan's friend chose a different area in the city centre. It offers excellent **nightlife** and many **cultural activities**, such as concerts and art shows. The **crime rate** is also very low. However, her rent is expensive and the tiny room is **poor value for money**. She has to **get the bus** to university every morning, and it is often late. Lan likes the ice-cream café on her street, where you can try **different flavours** like coconut, coffee and lychee. Now that exams are **just around the corner**, she is glad she can study close to home.

passages.title: From Entrance Test to Qualification
passages.text:
Hanh always dreamed of becoming a teacher, but the road was longer than she expected. She failed the entrance test the first time, so she studied harder and decided to **retake the exam** the following summer. This time she **got a place** at a university in Hue, where she began to **study for a degree** in English education.

During her first year, she **attended a lecture** almost every morning and took careful notes. She also joined a short evening class on classroom management. When she **completed the course successfully**, she was proud to **receive a certificate** from the head of the department. Employers often prefer applicants with an extra **qualification**, and Hanh knew that this certificate would help.

After four years of hard work, she finally **has a degree** in teaching, and she hopes to **qualify as** a primary school teacher next year. Some of her classmates thought it was impossible, but she **succeeded in passing** every exam. Her mother, who never went to university, says that a **qualified** teacher can change many lives. Hanh agrees, and she plans to continue learning throughout her career.
